climate.overview_html: Two new analytical entries anchor the September 16 climate update. Al Jazeera’s September 15 explainer “El Niño reaches super status” maps the confirmed Super El Niño’s regional impact geography: drought and intensified wildfire risk for Indonesia, the Philippines, Papua New Guinea, and eastern Australia (directly amplifying the ongoing ASEAN Level 3 haze emergency); above-normal flooding for the Horn of Africa, Peru, Ecuador, and the southern United States; and continued Atlantic hurricane suppression through November 2026. A September 14 analysis in The Diplomatic Affairs “Europe Just Had Its Hottest Summer on Record. The Costs Are Only Starting to Arrive” quantifies cascading economic damage: Rhine barge freight costs up 18–25% above seasonal norms; 2,025+ excess deaths in France; French farm income down ~9% from crop losses; Paks and Cernavodă nuclear plants curtailed by low river levels; western Europe averaged 2.54°C above the 1991–2020 normal — a record above even 2003. The underlying climate signals driving both stories remain unchanged: NOAA’s August 2026 report (September 12) confirming the warmest August in 177-year records at +1.32°C, Copernicus’ August 2026 bulletin at 1.65°C above pre-industrial — 16th consecutive month ≥1.5°C (September 10), and the Super El Niño RONI crossing +2.0°C on September 14.

items.headline: El Niño Reaches Super Status: Drought and Fire Risk for Indonesia, Philippines, Australia; Flooding for Horn of Africa, Peru, Southern U.S.; Atlantic Hurricane Suppression Continues Through November; 2027 Warmest Year Candidate >95% Probability
items.summary: Al Jazeera's September 15 regional impact explainer maps the coming teleconnection consequences of the confirmed Super El Niño (RONI +2.07°C as of September 14). Indonesia, the Philippines, Papua New Guinea, and eastern Australia face intensified drought and elevated wildfire risk through austral spring and summer 2026/27 — below-normal rainfall over Borneo directly amplifies the ongoing ASEAN Level 3 haze emergency. The Horn of Africa, equatorial East Africa, Peru, and Ecuador face above-normal precipitation and flooding risk in SON 2026 and DJF 2026/27. The Gulf Coast and southeastern United States face above-normal winter precipitation. Enhanced Eastern Pacific and Central Pacific tropical cyclone activity continues. The Atlantic Main Development Region remains suppressed through November by Super El Niño-driven vertical wind shear, extending the satellite-era hurricane drought. WMO assigns >95% probability to 2027 exceeding 2024 as the warmest year on record, as global temperature anomalies typically lag El Niño peak by 3–6 months.

items.headline: Europe Just Had Its Hottest Summer on Record — Western Europe 2.54°C Above 1991–2020 Normal; Rhine Freight Costs Up 18–25%; 2,025+ Excess Deaths France; Farm Income Down ~9%; Paks + Cernavodă Curtailed; “Costs Are Only Starting to Arrive”
items.summary: The Diplomatic Affairs analysis published September 14 quantifies the cascading economic and humanitarian damage of Europe's record summer 2026 — the hottest in recorded history for western Europe at 2.54°C above the 1991–2020 Copernicus climatology, surpassing the 2003 heat record. France recorded its hottest summer ever: 2,025+ excess deaths, with elevated mortality concentrated above age 45. The Rhine fell to its lowest navigational level since 1880, restricting barge traffic between Kaub and Cologne and pushing freight costs 18–25% above seasonal norms. Similar Danube low-water constraints forced Hungary's Paks-2 nuclear plant and Romania's Cernavodă nuclear plant to curtailed output. French farm income declined approximately 9% from crop failures. The analysis notes these headline tallies exclude longer-term infrastructure damage, ecosystem impacts, health system strain, and the productivity losses that compound over months and years — hence costs 'are only starting to arrive.'

items.headline: NOAA NCEI August 2026 Global Climate Report: Warmest August in 177-Year Record at +1.32°C (+2.38°F); Breaks Prior 2023–2024 Tied Record by 0.08°C; JJA 2026 Warmest Meteorological Summer Globally; 2026 On Track for Warmest Calendar Year
items.summary: NOAA's National Centers for Environmental Information confirmed August 2026 as the warmest August in 177 years of instrumental records at +1.32°C (+2.38°F) above the 20th-century average, breaking the previous tied record shared by August 2023 and August 2024 by 0.08°C. Meteorological summer (JJA) 2026 was the warmest on record globally at +1.21°C above the 20th-century average. Northern Hemisphere land temperatures were highest on record for any August; ocean surface temperatures were second-highest. Year-to-date (January–August 2026) global temperatures are the warmest in the 177-year dataset, placing 2026 on trajectory to become the warmest calendar year ever recorded — further elevated by the Super El Niño peak forecast for November–January 2026/27.

items.headline: Copernicus August 2026 Bulletin: Joint-Hottest Month on Record (Tied July 2023) at 1.65°C Above Pre-Industrial; Extra-Polar SSTs All-Time August Record 21.07°C; 13.2% of Global Surfaces Set Record-High August Temperatures; 16th Consecutive Month ≥1.5°C
items.summary: Copernicus Climate Change Service's September 10 monthly bulletin confirms August 2026 as the world's joint-hottest month on record, tied with July 2023 at 1.65°C above the pre-industrial baseline (1850–1900 average). August 2026 was the 16th consecutive month at or above the 1.5°C Paris Agreement threshold. Extra-polar sea surface temperatures set an all-time August record at 21.07°C. 13.2% of global land and ocean surfaces registered record-high temperatures for any August day during the month. The joint-record status means the three hottest months in recorded history now include two months from 2026: tying July 2023 and August 2026.

items.headline: Super El Niño Confirmed: Running ONI Crosses +2.0°C September 14 — First Super El Niño Since 2015–16; CNN: “Super El Niño Is Actually Here Now”; Peak Forecast NDJ 2026/27 at +2.4–2.8°C; WMO >95% Probability 2027 Sets Warmest Year Record
items.summary: The Running Oceanic Niño Index (RONI) crossed the +2.0°C threshold on September 14, 2026, officially qualifying the current event as a Super El Niño — the first since 2015–16, which peaked at +2.6°C. The RONI reached +2.07°C. NOAA and WMO multi-model ensembles forecast a peak of +2.4–2.8°C for November–January 2026/27, with some ensemble members reaching +3.0°C. Continued Atlantic hurricane suppression, drought in eastern Australia and SE Asia, and enhanced precipitation in the Horn of Africa are the primary near-term impacts. WMO assigns >95% probability to 2027 exceeding 2024 as the warmest year on record.

items.headline: Nepal–Tibet Glacier Collapse Floods: ~1,429 Dead (1,386 Nepal + 43 Tibet); ~5,649+ Missing Including 587 Foreign Nationals; $820M+ Pledged; Nepal Parliament Declares National Climate Emergency; Ongoing Humanitarian Response
items.summary: As of September 12, Nepal's NDRRMA confirmed approximately 1,386 deaths in Nepal and 43 in Tibet — approximately 1,429 total — with approximately 5,649 persons missing including 587 foreign nationals from 34 countries. International pledges have reached $820 million. Nepal's parliament declared a national climate emergency on September 12, citing accelerating climate-driven glacial loss; a formal UNFCCC Loss and Damage Fund submission has been initiated. ICIMOD found the Yanmarang Glacier lost approximately 40% of its volume in the 2020s. Humanitarian response and recovery operations remain active. The event is the deadliest glacier-related disaster in recorded Himalayan history.

weather.overview_html: The key operational update on September 16 is Pakistan: NDMA issued a national flood alert September 15 for Gilgit-Baltistan, KPK, Punjab, and Balochistan with heavy rainfall forecast through September 17, and the monsoon death toll has risen to 234 dead / 596 injured — up from 183 / 515 on September 11. In the Western Pacific, Invest 90W is inside its 48-hour JTWC High TCFA development window (issued 0600Z September 15); tropical depression status is imminent and forecast before 0600Z September 17, with the system expected to intensify to Typhoon Dujuan around September 19–20, posing an Okinawa/Kyushu impact risk September 20–22. The Atlantic hurricane season has extended its satellite-era record to 108+ consecutive days without a hurricane; the central subtropical Atlantic trough has a 40% 7-day formation probability but no MDR development is forecast. Ongoing: SE Asia ASEAN Level 3 haze emergency, Nepal-Tibet flood response (~1,429 dead), and Europe wildfires (~660,528 ha per EFFIS September 9).

items.source: Pakistan NDMA / The Express Tribune / Gulf News
items.headline: Pakistan NDMA Flood Alert September 15: Rainfall Through September 17 Across GB, KPK, Punjab, Balochistan; Monsoon Death Toll Updated to 234+ Dead / 596+ Injured — Urban Flooding Ongoing + GB Landslide Deaths
items.summary: Pakistan's NDMA issued a flood alert September 15, warning that heavy monsoon rainfall through September 17 in Gilgit-Baltistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab, and Balochistan could trigger widespread flooding and landslides. Specific flash flood risks cover GB's Gilgit, Diamer, Ghizer, Nagar, Hunza, Skardu, and Shigar districts, and KPK's Upper Dir, Swat, Bajaur, Malakand, and Kohistan. Gulf News reported the nationwide monsoon death toll has risen to 234 dead and 596 injured since the monsoon opened in late June — up from 183 dead / 515 injured as of September 11. Three additional people were killed in landslides in Gilgit-Baltistan on September 15, with 15 missing after tourist vehicles were swept away. PMD's forecast peak period of September 14–17 continues; urban flooding is ongoing across Lahore, Faisalabad, and Rawalpindi.

items.headline: Invest 90W: 48-H JTWC Development Window Active September 16 — TD Status Imminent Before 0600Z September 17; Typhoon Dujuan Forecast ~September 19–20; ECMWF Cat 2–3 by Weekend; Okinawa / Kyushu Landfall Risk September 20–22
items.summary: Invest 90W is inside the active 48-hour tropical cyclone development window following the JTWC Tropical Cyclone Formation Alert (HIGH) issued at 0600Z September 15. The disturbance, tracking WNW over sea surface temperatures of 29.5–31.0°C with reduced vertical wind shear, is on track for tropical depression status before 0600Z September 17. Upon reaching tropical storm intensity, the system will be designated Typhoon Dujuan by JMA. ECMWF ensemble guidance shows approximately 68% of members reaching Category 2–3 (≥70–95 kt) typhoon strength by Saturday September 19, with the track curving NNW toward potential Okinawa and Kyushu landfall or close passage September 20–22. SSTs along the projected track are significantly above the rapid intensification threshold, consistent with Super El Niño-suppressed upwelling in the subtropical Western Pacific.

items.source: ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre / Antara / ABC Australia / Al Jazeera
items.headline: SE Asia Haze ONGOING: ASEAN Level 3 Transboundary Alert; ~300,000 ha Active Fires Kalimantan; >5 Million People Directly Exposed; 1.4 Million Malaysian Students Remote; Below-Normal Rainfall Through October; Super El Niño Amplifying Dry Season
items.summary: The ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre's Level 3 transboundary haze alert remains in force. Approximately 300,000 hectares of active fires in Kalimantan generate PM2.5 concentrations above 500 µg/m³ in parts of Sarawak and Brunei. More than 5 million people across Borneo and Sumatra are directly exposed to health risks. Malaysia has kept 1.4 million students in remote learning. Indonesia's BNPB maintains approximately 12,000 firefighting personnel and water-bombing aircraft. Fires have released an estimated 23+ million metric tons of CO₂ equivalent between late August and early September. Below-normal rainfall is forecast across the southern ASEAN region through October, directly driven by the confirmed Super El Niño amplifying the Maritime Continent dry season — exactly as Al Jazeera's September 15 impact mapping predicted.

items.headline: Europe Wildfires ONGOING: ~660,528 ha Burned Per EFFIS September 9; Rhine at 1880 Historic Low; Paks + Cernavodă Nuclear Curtailed; Western Europe’s Hottest Summer on Record 2.54°C Above Climatology; Cascading Economic Costs Emerging
items.summary: EFFIS updated the 2026 European wildfire total to approximately 660,528 hectares as of September 9 — the worst season since 2017. Western Europe's record summer (2.54°C above the 1991–2020 average) has created exceptional fire conditions; extreme fire danger continues in the Iberian Peninsula, Pyrenees, and western Balkans. The Rhine remains at its lowest navigational level since 1880, restricting barge traffic between Kaub and Cologne and pushing freight costs 18–25% above seasonal norms. Hungary's Paks-2 nuclear plant and Romania's Cernavodă plant are at curtailed output due to low Danube water. The co-occurrence of wildfire, drought, flash flooding, and heatwave deaths represents the compound climate risk profile of the 2026 Super El Niño / global heat event, with cascading economic impacts only beginning to be quantified.

items.headline: Atlantic Hurricane Season: 108+ Consecutive Days Without a Hurricane as of September 16 — Satellite-Era Record Extended; Central Subtropical Trough at 40% 7-Day Formation Probability; No Imminent MDR Development; El Niño Shear Dominant
items.summary: The 2026 Atlantic hurricane season has gone 108+ consecutive days without producing a hurricane as of September 16, extending the satellite-era record reported September 11 at 103 days and September 15 at 107 days. Five named tropical storms have formed this season; none has reached hurricane strength. NOAA's September 16 Tropical Weather Outlook identifies a central subtropical Atlantic trough approximately 800 miles ESE of Bermuda with 40% formation probability in 7 days — the most active area of interest but with no imminent Main Development Region development. NOAA's updated season forecast of 7–13 named storms and 2–6 hurricanes reflects ongoing Super El Niño-driven vertical wind shear over the MDR, a teleconnection pattern expected to persist through November 2026.

renewables.overview_html: Three new milestones define the September 16 renewables update. The UK Secretary of State approved the Development Consent Order for transmission assets of both the 480 MW Morecambe and co-located Morgan offshore wind farms on September 14–15 — completing full regulatory consent for Morecambe (generation DCO granted December 2025) and covering all offshore export cables, substations, and grid connection infrastructure to the Penwortham substation. Econergy Ltd acquired Escofi — a private French 740 MW onshore wind platform — for €134.3 million on September 15, adding 128 MW in operation, 34 MW under construction, and 578 MW in development, with >90% of operational capacity under 20-year French CfDs above €80/MWh. Masdar and Luxcara signed an MoU September 14 to jointly invest in excess of €5 billion in German battery storage and offshore wind — announced during the UAE state visit to Berlin and potentially expandable beyond Germany. The previous window’s flagship transactions remain in scope: Gennaker 976.5 MW financial close (€3 billion+, Amazon 600 MW PPA), Enel’s $760 million U.S. solar acquisition (810 MW), and India’s 16.39 GW renewable additions in April–July 2026 tracking ~50 GW annually.

items.headline: UK Secretary of State Approves DCO for Morecambe (480 MW) + Morgan Offshore Wind Transmission Assets — Full Consent Package Completed; Offshore Export Cables, Substations + Grid to Penwortham; >500,000 UK Households; East Irish Sea
items.summary: UK Secretary of State for Energy Security and Net Zero approved the Development Consent Order for transmission assets serving both the 480 MW Morecambe and co-located Morgan offshore wind farms on September 14, announced by the Planning Inspectorate on September 15. The consent covers offshore export cables, landfall infrastructure, onshore cables, substations, circuit-breaker compounds, and grid connection to the National Grid substation at Penwortham, Lancashire. Morecambe, developed by Copenhagen Offshore Partners for Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners approximately 30 km off the Lancashire coast, received its generation DCO in December 2025; today's transmission consent completes the full regulatory package. The 35-turbine project will power over 500,000 UK households. The joint transmission DCO also covers the separately re-tendered Morgan project, which will share infrastructure and grid connection alongside Morecambe.

items.source: Renewable Energy Magazine / reNEWS / Yahoo Finance / Energy Global
items.headline: Econergy Acquires Escofi — 740 MW French Onshore Wind Platform for €134.3 Million: 128 MW Operational, 34 MW Under Construction, 578 MW in Development; >90% Operating Capacity Under 20-Year French CfDs at >€80/MWh; Econergy’s Entry Into France
items.summary: Econergy Ltd acquired Escofi, a private French onshore wind developer and operator founded in 1988, for €134.3 million on September 15, marking Econergy's entry into France. Escofi's 740 MW portfolio comprises 128 MW in commercial operation, 34 MW under construction (operations by 2027), 147 MW in advanced development with building permits and grid approvals secured (construction 2028–2030), and 432 MW in early-to-mid development. More than 90% of operational and under-construction capacity benefits from 20-year Contracts for Difference under France's CfD regime at prices above €80/MWh. In July 2026, Escofi secured additional CfDs for three further projects totalling 46 MW. The acquisition expands Econergy's European wind portfolio alongside existing assets in Poland, Romania, and the UK.

items.source: offshoreWIND.biz / Energy Storage News / Energy Global
items.headline: Masdar + Luxcara Sign €5 Billion+ MoU for Germany Battery Storage and Offshore Wind — Signed During UAE State Visit to Berlin; Potential Expansion Beyond Germany; Masdar Advances UAE–Europe Energy Partnership
items.summary: Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company (Masdar) and Luxcara, an independent German clean energy asset manager, signed an MoU September 14 to explore a joint investment in excess of €5 billion in battery energy storage systems and offshore wind projects in Germany, announced during the UAE state visit to Berlin. The partnership targets co-development, financing, and ownership of large-scale BESS and offshore wind infrastructure, with possible expansion to other European markets. Masdar brings sovereign-backed scale and an existing German pipeline; Luxcara contributes domestic market expertise and established grid-connection relationships. Germany's battery storage market is expanding rapidly as 2026 offshore wind tenders require co-located BESS. The MoU remains subject to definitive agreements and customary regulatory approvals.

items.headline: Skyborn Renewables + Stadtwerke München Close €3 Billion+ Financing for 976.5 MW Gennaker Offshore Wind Farm (German Baltic Sea) — Amazon 600 MW PPA; Uniper 100 MW PPA; SWM 25% Equity; Target Commercial Operations End-2028
items.summary: Skyborn Renewables and Stadtwerke München reached financial close on September 11 for the 976.5 MW Gennaker offshore wind farm in the German Baltic Sea. The financing totals €2.1 billion non-recourse project finance from 16 commercial lenders and the European Investment Bank, mobilising more than €3 billion total investment. Long-term PPAs include 600 MW to Amazon and 100 MW to Uniper. SWM holds a 25% equity stake. The 63-turbine Siemens Gamesa project is expected to generate approximately 3.8 TWh annually (around one million German households), targeting commercial operations end-2028.

items.headline: Enel Green Power Acquires Faraday (682 MW DC, Utah) + Skyhawk (128 MW DC, Tennessee) From Excelsior Energy Capital for $760 Million — PacifiCorp 20-Year PPA; Meta Energy Off-take; TVA Contract
items.summary: Excelsior Energy Capital completed the $760 million sale of the Faraday Solar Plant (682 MW DC / 525 MW AC, Utah County, Utah — 20-year PacifiCorp PPA with Meta purchasing energy attributes) and Skyhawk Solar Plant (~128 MW DC, Obion County, Tennessee — Tennessee Valley Authority long-term PPA) to Enel Green Power North America on September 11. Combined ~810 MW DC / 625 MW AC of contracted U.S. solar capacity, expanding Enel Green Power's footprint in PJM and TVA service territories.

items.headline: India Renewable Additions: 16.39 GW in April–July 2026 (14.33 GW Solar + 2.04 GW Wind); BESS Growing Faster Than Generation; On Track for ~50 GW Annual FY2026–27
items.summary: India added 16.39 GW of renewable energy capacity in the first four months of FY2026–27 (April–July 2026): 14.33 GW solar PV and 2.04 GW wind. Battery energy storage system additions are growing on a percentage basis faster than either solar or wind, reflecting the MNRE push to pair storage with intermittent generation. The April–July run rate places India on track for approximately 50 GW of annual additions in FY2026–27, which would be a record and sustain India's position as the third-largest global renewable market.

science.overview_html: The week’s leading new science publication is in climate physics: Brönnimann, Brugnara, and Kallabis published “A strengthening yet less extreme Atlantic–European jet during winter” in Nature Geoscience on September 10, 2026 — a 300-year instrumental record analysis (1725–2100) finding the jet has already strengthened by 0.13 standard deviations since pre-industrial and is projected to continue strengthening under RCP8.5 through 2100, while simultaneously exhibiting less frequent extremes in speed, latitude, and tilt; the counterintuitive finding implies a potential reduction in the most destructive European windstorms and blocking-driven heat waves even as mean circulation strengthens. In AI weather modeling, the dominant window preprint remains arXiv:2609.12815 (BEAST, September 11) — a Bayesian Ensemble AI Swin Transformer trained on JUPITER’s 20,480 NVIDIA GH200 GPUs that produces 96-member weight-space ensemble forecasts competitive with ECMWF AIFS and operational NWP on extreme weather metrics. arXiv:2609.11696 (September 10) delivers the definitive head-to-head stress test of WRF dynamical versus diffusion-model generative downscaling for subseasonal extreme precipitation at 3-week lead times, directly relevant to the Pakistan and European flash-flood events now active. arXiv:2609.08241 EastAsiaClimateExtremes (September 8) provides the first AI-ready weekly S2S benchmark for East Asian atmospheric and oceanic extremes including the heat, heavy-rainfall, and marine heatwave regimes driving this digest period’s major weather events.

items.headline: Nature Geoscience: “A Strengthening Yet Less Extreme Atlantic–European Jet During Winter” — 300-Year Record (1725–2100); Jet Has Already Strengthened 0.13 SD Since Pre-Industrial; Projected to Continue Strengthening But With Fewer Extreme Jet Excursions; Implications for European Windstorms, Heat Waves, Blocking
items.meta: Brönnimann, Brugnara & Kallabis · Nature Geoscience (2026) · doi:10.1038/s41561-026-02069-z · Published 10 September 2026
items.summary: Brönnimann, Brugnara, and Kallabis present a 300-year analysis of daily Atlantic–European jet stream variability from 1725 to 2100 using four long European pressure station records combined with climate model ensemble projections. Since the pre-industrial period the jet has strengthened by 0.13 standard deviations and shifted poleward in the cold season. Future projections under continued warming show continued strengthening through 2100, but with extremes in jet speed, latitude, and tilt becoming less frequent — the counterintuitive result that a stronger jet has reduced variance in its most anomalous states. The study also captures solar storm and sudden stratospheric warming signals. The key implication: the most destructive European windstorms and the most persistent blocking-driven heat waves (of the type that defined western Europe's record summer 2026) may become less frequent even as mean circulation intensifies, though uncertainties in blocking-regime projections remain large. Relevant context: the record 2026 European heatwave represents exactly the type of persistent blocking event the paper's projections suggest may become rarer.

items.source: arXiv / Jülich Supercomputing Centre / JUPITER / Helmholtz AI
items.headline: arXiv 2609.12815 (BEAST): Bayesian Ensemble AI Swin Transformer Trained on JUPITER (20,480 NVIDIA GH200 GPUs, 3.96 EFLOP/s); 700M Parameters; 96-Member Weight-Space Ensemble; Competitive With ECMWF AIFS and NWP on Extreme Weather Metrics
items.summary: BEAST (Bayesian Ensemble AI Swin Transformer) is trained on the JUPITER supercomputer — the first exaflop-class European HPC system — using 20,480 NVIDIA GH200 Grace Hopper Superchips across 10,240 nodes at 3.96 EFLOP/s distributed throughput. The 700-million-parameter model generates 96 ensemble members via weight-space sampling, producing calibrated probabilistic outputs without the overhead of explicit multi-model ensembles. On benchmark evaluations for extreme weather events, BEAST achieves skill competitive with ECMWF's AI Integrated Forecasting System (AIFS) and operational NWP ensemble systems. The Bayesian ensemble approach directly addresses the central limitation of deterministic AI weather models: underrepresentation of forecast uncertainty for low-probability high-impact events — directly relevant to the Pakistan monsoon flooding, European flash floods, and imminent Typhoon Dujuan development being tracked this digest period.

items.source: arXiv / Bjerknes Centre for Climate Research / University of Bergen
items.headline: arXiv 2609.11696: WRF Dynamical vs Diffusion-Model Generative Downscaling for Subseasonal Extreme Precipitation at 3-Week Lead Times — WRF Wins on Non-Stationary Multicell Events; Diffusion More Consistent on Stationary Supercells; Both Beat Raw ECMWF
items.summary: This paper evaluates WRF dynamical downscaling head-to-head against a diffusion-based deep generative model by downscaling ECMWF subseasonal forecasts for two physically distinct extreme precipitation events at lead times up to 3 weeks. Both approaches substantially improve on raw ECMWF outputs. WRF achieves the highest probabilistic skill for a multicell non-stationary event — the character of the September 10–11 Mediterranean outbreak (203 mm/24h at Lignano Sabbiadoro) where the dynamical core's explicit physics captures large-scale forcing. The diffusion model outperforms WRF on a more stationary supercell event and is more consistent across metrics overall, suggesting regime-adaptive or ensemble downscaling frameworks rather than a single fixed approach for operational extreme precipitation prediction at S2S timescales.

items.source: arXiv / Fudan University / ECMWF / Chinese Academy of Sciences
items.headline: arXiv 2609.08241 (EastAsiaClimateExtremes): First AI-Ready Weekly S2S Benchmark for East Asian Atmospheric and Oceanic Extremes — Anomalous Heat, Heavy Rainfall, Marine Heatwaves; Co-Registered With ECMWF S2S Hindcasts; Open on GitHub
items.summary: EastAsiaClimateExtremes provides an open benchmark dataset with ERA5/OISST reanalysis-based weekly extreme labels for anomalously high temperature, heavy rainfall, and marine heatwaves over East Asia, co-registered with ECMWF S2S hindcast outputs to enable direct comparison between AI forecasts and dynamical sub-seasonal models. The dataset addresses a critical gap: event-based AI-ready datasets for East Asia at S2S timescales — where dynamical models face the largest skill gaps — have been sparse. Direct relevance: the SE Asia haze emergency, Pakistan monsoon peak, and Super El Niño IOD co-evolution are exactly the S2S phenomena this benchmark targets. Available at GitHub.

items.title: Masdar + Luxcara Sign €5 Billion+ MoU for Germany Battery Storage and Offshore Wind — UAE State Visit to Berlin; Sovereign-Backed Scale Meets Domestic Market Expertise; Potential European Expansion
items.body_html: Abu Dhabi Future Energy Company (Masdar) and Luxcara, an independent German clean energy asset manager, signed a Memorandum of Understanding on September 14 to explore a joint investment in excess of €5 billion in battery energy storage systems and offshore wind projects in Germany, announced during the UAE state visit to Berlin. The MoU targets co-development, financing, and ownership of large-scale BESS and offshore wind projects in Germany, with potential expansion to other European markets; it remains subject to definitive agreements and customary regulatory approvals. Masdar brings sovereign-backed scale — it has announced an existing German pipeline exceeding €8 billion across offshore wind and storage — while Luxcara contributes domestic market expertise, established grid-connection relationships, and a track record in German renewable infrastructure financing. Germany’s 2026 offshore wind tender framework requires co-located BESS, making the partnership structurally well-positioned for the next tender round.
items.source_html: offshoreWIND.biz / Energy Storage News

items.title: Premier Energies + RCT India Form 12 GWh BESS Manufacturing Joint Venture in Telangana — India’s Largest Planned Battery Storage Manufacturing Partnership; Rides BESS Policy Push Alongside 16.39 GW FY2026–27 Renewable Additions
items.body_html: Premier Energies, the Hyderabad-based publicly listed solar cell and module manufacturer, and RCT India, a battery energy storage system developer, announced a joint venture on September 11 to manufacture 12 GWh of battery energy storage systems annually at a new facility in Telangana. The partnership positions Premier Energies to extend its supply-chain integration from solar PV manufacturing into the adjacent BESS market, at a moment when India’s BESS capacity additions are growing faster on a percentage basis than either solar or wind generation — reflecting MNRE’s push to pair storage mandatorily with large-scale renewable plants. The 12 GWh annual manufacturing target, if realised, would represent one of the largest domestically manufactured BESS pipelines in India and would directly serve accelerating state-level procurement tenders for grid-scale storage across Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Telangana.

items.title: Perry Weather Raises $110 Million Growth Investment From Silversmith Capital Partners — Hyperlocal Weather Safety Platform Covers 3,000+ Organizations; 50+ Dallas Hires Planned; Total Funding $131 Million
items.body_html: Perry Weather, the Dallas-based hyperlocal weather safety and operations platform, closed a $110 million growth investment on September 9, led by Silversmith Capital Partners with participation from prior investor Arthur Ventures; total funding reaches $131.35 million. Perry Weather pairs purpose-built on-site hardware weather stations with AI-assisted cloud software delivering real-time hyperlocal monitoring, automated alerts, and siren activation covering lightning, extreme heat, high wind, and air quality across more than 3,000 organizations including school districts, municipalities, construction firms, manufacturers, and major professional sports leagues. The company will add 50+ roles through 2027 at its Dallas headquarters. The round reflects enterprise demand for site-specific alerting at a time when the frequency of high-impact convective events is driving corporate and government weather-safety investment.
items.source_html: Yahoo Finance / Dallas Innovates

items.title: WINT Water Intelligence Raises $36 Million Series D to Scale AI-Powered Water Management Globally — LIP Ventures and Inven Capital Co-Lead; 30,000+ Systems Installed; 1.15 Billion Gallons Saved; $100 Million in Water-Damage Losses Prevented in 2025
items.body_html: WINT Water Intelligence closed a $36 million Series D on September 9, co-led by LIP Ventures and Inven Capital (a €500 million European climate tech fund backed by CEZ Group), with participation from Insight Partners and others; total funding now approximately $105 million. WINT’s AI platform detects and prevents water waste and damage in commercial buildings in real time, covering more than 30,000 installed systems across nearly 600 enterprise customers; in 2025 it saved 1.15 billion gallons of water and prevented an estimated $100 million in potential water-damage losses across more than 1,300 incidents. The platform is increasingly positioned as a climate adaptation tool for property and casualty insurers: water damage from extreme-weather-linked precipitation events is a rapidly rising loss category, directly relevant given the European flash floods and Pakistan monsoon flooding tracked in this digest.
